# AGENTS.md — 18-space-museum

Instructions for AI coding agents working in this folder.

## Context
- Template: **Kepler Hall**, space museum, style "Printed star atlas".
- Stack: Vanilla JS, Three.js, Vite. Do not add dependencies unless the user asks.
- The design contract is in `DESIGN.md`. Read it before changing anything visual.

## Files
- `src/content.js` — constellations, exhibits, shows, all copy (EN + RU)
- `src/sky.js` — star coordinates, stick figures, moon phase
- `src/sphere.js` — Three.js celestial sphere
- `src/main.js` — rendering, language, moon
- `src/style.css` — tokens at the top

## How to run
- `npm install`
- `npm run dev`
- `npm run build   # ./dist`

## Rules
- Content changes go to the content file, not into markup or components.
- Every user-facing string exists in **en** and **ru**. English is the default; `?lang=ru` and the language button switch it.
- Colors, fonts, radii and spacing are tokens. Change tokens, not individual elements.
- Keep the signature block: Draggable 3D celestial sphere drawn as an atlas plate — RA/Dec grid, real constellations; pick one and the sky turns to it.
- Keep accessibility: semantic headings, visible focus, alt text, `prefers-reduced-motion` support, body text contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
- Keep it static: no backend, no booking or payment flows.
- Space is blue plates on paper, never a full-screen black void.
- Star positions are real (J2000 approx.) — add stars with RA hours and Dec degrees in sky.js.
- Gold marks only the selected constellation.
- Old Standard TT for headings and captions, PT Sans for UI.
- Three.js is lazy-loaded; the page works without WebGL.

## Done means
- The page builds/opens without console errors.
- Both languages render with no missing strings.
- Layout works from 360 px to 1920 px wide.
